failures.criterion: Acceptance 1: after docker stop of the rig's NATS container, re-running up.sh with the same environment prints `STARTED NATS container <name>` and reaches `RIG READY`
failures.evidence: Run 2 (same env and SMOKE_DIR, container stopped) printed `STARTED NATS container legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar870` through the docker start path (same container: Created 17:48:50Z, StartedAt 17:49:38Z) then `REUSED listener (pid 1680779)` and `error: Envoy listener did not become healthy; inspect /tmp/legion-smoke-87`, exit 1 — RIG READY not reached. The reused listener reconnected to NATS (`envoy nats recovery successful attempt=4`) but every self-health probe kept failing with `interest kv: nats: connection closed`; it logged `self-health terminal failure threshold exceeded; terminating for restart` at 17:50:50Z and exited. Cause is the Envoy listener's rebuild not recreating the interest KV handle on the new connection (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go rebuildListenerDependencies; inference from log and code), pre-existing and outside scripts/smoke; filed as LEGION-120. Supplementary run 3, reboot-shaped (listener and my own daemon down, container stopped): `STARTED NATS container legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar870` (docker start, same container) → `STARTED listener` → `STARTED daemon` → `RIG READY`, exit 0.

surface: Real smoke rig on this box driven through scripts/smoke/up.sh and down.sh. Own rig: SMOKE_PROJECT=sjawhar/870 (container legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar870), SMOKE_DIR=/tmp/legion-smoke-87, NATS_PORT=14870, ENVOY_PORT=19070, LEGION_DAEMON_PORT=19870, SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=none, secrets via the README's `secrets ENVOY_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 -- bash -c '…'` wrapper, DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN from envoy.json. The other live rig (legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar1083, 14283) untouched. Root issue created by the rig: LEGSMOKE-190.

acceptance.1: FAIL — STARTED line yes (docker start path), RIG READY no; see failures[0] and LEGION-120
acceptance.2: PASS — up.test.sh stopped+other-port case (up.test.sh:955) and the real-surface negative control
acceptance.3: PASS — down.test.sh stopped+matching-port case (down.test.sh:230) asserts rm -f through the inspect reads; no legacy container fabricated

observations: The script change is correct: the ownership test recognises the stopped container (created-with binding), docker start is reached, the same container (same Created time, JetStream state kept) comes back; the refusal names both ports and starts nothing.

Acceptance 1's check (docker stop only, listener and daemon alive) exercises a path the issue's reboot scenario does not: a listener that survives a NATS outage. That listener never returns to healthy and exits after ~110 s (LEGION-120), so up.sh's 60 s /healthz poll on the REUSED listener fails. Options for the architect: treat LEGION-120 as the blocker, or have up.sh restart a listener whose /healthz is not healthy instead of reusing it (scripts/smoke scope), or restate the check as the reboot-shaped sequence — not the tester's call.

The rig's daemon logs nothing about its own NATS disconnect/reconnect (daemon.log had only the two listening lines); whether the daemon's NATS connection recovers after an outage was not observable here and is not part of this issue.
PR #1056 is MERGEABLE (not CONFLICTING); no rebase. Evidence transcript attached to LEGION-87 as tester-transcript-pr1056.md.

The outer Legion daemon (127.0.0.1:13370) was down from about 17:52Z during this phase, blocking the pane's bash grant mint; rig operations continued through the Python kernel (secrets agent-tier keys resolved without a session).
documentationFeedback: README's reuse sentence (`a stopped one … is started with STARTED NATS container <name>`) matches what the surface prints. Nothing else to change for this issue.
